content.body:
![Colorful painted mural depicting a black woman with her arms outstreched and flowers in her hair](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4998)

## Project background

In July 2021, Arvada hosted the second Babe Walls festival, a unique celebration of women and non-binary mural artists. Over four days, 26 artists — local and from across the country — collaborated to create a series of connected murals along the Ralston Creek Trail in east Arvada.

## Where to find the murals

The Babe Walls murals are located along the Ralston Creek Trail [underpass at the intersection of Lamar Street and Ralston Road](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mVNyUJUX45UWEdhj8). This section of Arvada’s popular off-street trail features vibrant, large-scale artwork that stretches more than 200 yards long.

These murals bring beauty and energy to the area, creating a colorful, artful experience that enhances walkability and connects to the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission's goal of ensuring every resident has access to public art within a 10-minute walk.

## Babe Walls 2024 refresh

In 2024 artist Danielle SeeWalker refreshed a section of the Babe Walls Arvada murals after they were in need of repair. SeeWalker, who was also part of the 2021 Babe Walls Arvada Festival, said the new murals were inspired by her Lakota heritage. One of the new murals features bright pop-art women along with traditional Lakota patterns and designs; the other mural depicts the life of a Lakota warrior from birth to death.

![Babe Walls artist Danielle SeeWalker](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4999)

### About Babe Walls

[Babe Walls is an annual mural festival](https://www.babewalls.com/) dedicated to empowering women and non-binary artists in the traditionally male-dominated world of street art. What sets this festival apart is its emphasis on collaboration. Each mural is a team effort, pairing experienced artists with emerging talent to foster mentorship and creativity.

The festival also serves as a platform for inclusivity, offering a safe and supportive space for artists to explore their craft, connect with their peers, and inspire future generations.

### Babe Walls in Arvada

Arvada partnered with Babe Walls and multiple city departments, including the Parks, Trails, and Bike and Pedestrian teams, to bring this vibrant festival to life. The festival took place July 15–18, 2021, leaving behind not just beautiful murals but a lasting sense of community and collaboration.

Babe Walls Arvada Artists are below. [Visit the Babe Walls Arvada page to view each mural](https://www.babewalls.com/2021-arvada).

Learn more about the Babe Walls festival and hear directly from the artists by watching these videos:

- [Babe Walls 2021 Documentary](https://youtu.be/HCashp5wm2w?feature=shared)
- [Babe Walls Arvada Project Background](https://youtu.be/mVbLWn6sNqo?feature=shared)

## Explore the murals today

Visit the Lamar Street underpass and surrounding trails to see the murals for yourself. These artworks are a testament to the power of creativity, inclusivity, and community collaboration in Arvada.
